Two 100GbE QSFP28 ports on the front beside a console and two management jacks, behind a built-in bezel, with a touch screen beside it; two hot-swap 550W supplies and a one-piece five-fan tray on the back, front-to-back.","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"WHAT THE LAMPS MEAN IS UNKNOWN. The slot left of port 0 is one light-pipe opening (photographed square-on), and the vendor's UI view draws four lamps in a column there; all four carry `for: chassis`. The maintainer counts one lamp per 100G port, and the photograph shows no lamp anywhere else near the ports, so two of the four are probably those - but nothing says which, and an invented mapping would be worse than none. The chassis status lamp on the bezel beside the right window is modelled. Red and green points seen through the louvres in the rack photograph are internal board LEDs and are deliberately not drawn. The touch screen is maiaedge/pbc-2000-lcd@2 and what it shows is software.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["front"],"wanted":"an LED table, or a photograph of the unit powered up with the transceivers out.","what":"front-indicator-meanings"},{"note":"These four faces draw the chassis envelope and nothing else. The envelope itself is not a guess - 437.90 x 291.08 x 41.27 is dimensioned on page 3 of the datasheet - but no source held shows what is ON any of them: no vent field, no label, no screw pattern, no rail. The flat rect asserts the box and claims nothing about its surface, which is what lets the device carry a rack elevation and a 3D box without inventing detail.","reason":"needs-photo","scope":["top","bottom","left","right"],"wanted":"photographs of the lid, the underside and either flank out of the rack. The unit was shot in service with a device directly above it.","what":"envelope-faces-undetailed"},{"note":"The datasheet states the supply configuration and no chassis draw figure, so none is recorded. L27 stands, and the chassis total is a floor rather than a total.","reason":"vendor-silent","wanted":"a chassis draw or input figure from MaiaEdge.","what":"chassis-power-draw"}],"groups":{"displays":{"index-origin":1,"role":"indicator","term":"Display"},"fans":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Fan"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Part"},"mgmt":{"index-origin":1,"mixed":"the console and the two out-of-band management jacks, which share a bezel","role":"management","term":"Port"},"psus":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"1+1","redundancy-note":"datasheet page 3, \"Redundant Power Supply: Yes\"; the setup guide, \"equipped with two redundant AC power inputs\""},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PSU"},"qsfp28":{"attrs":{"media":"qsfp28","speed":"100g"},"index-origin":0,"role":"traffic","term":"Port"}},"kind":"device","manufacturer":"MaiaEdge","maturity":"modelled","model":"PBC-2000","name":"pbc-2000","profile":"networking","provenance":{"bezel":{"confidence":"estimated","note":"ESTIMATED shape, from photographs and the maintainer's account of the hardware (2026-09-21), and since v5 photo-measured in plan. The front is a BUILT-IN BEZEL standing about 11 mm off the faceplate, from the left edge to the touch screen, with the two OCTAGONAL windows cut through it: the octagons frame the faceplate behind, where the ports are. It is flat only across the band level with the windows' vertical ends, and slopes back to the faceplate above and below. That plate is maiaedge/pbc-2000-bezel@2 and its own provenance carries the figures. v3 drew the slope as shading on a flat face; the window walls are the amber bead, which is what looking into a window shows. THE OCTAGONS ARE NOT REGULAR: the face-on photograph puts each chamfer at about 19 mm across for 13 down, where `shape: octagon` cuts 45 degrees. So the windows are no longer decor shapes at all - they are holes in the bezel's own art, drawn to the measured corners."},"cutouts":{"confidence":"registry","note":"registry - each opening is the APERTURE the component declares, not the component's outline: common/qsfp-cage@2 is 19.5 x 10.18 of metal around an 18.5 x 9.58 hole offset (0.575, 0.6) into it, and a USB-A is 17.0 x 9.3 around a 12.0 x 4.5 hole at (2.5, 2.4). The first draft punched the outlines and test_cutout_derivation caught all three."},"jack-height":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"THE JACKS ARE DRAWN 1.1 MM HIGHER THAN THE PHOTOGRAPH PUTS THEM, deliberately. The photograph shows each jack's opening 10.3 mm tall between its caption above (y 20.1 to 22.7) and \"1G\" below (y 35.1 to 36.6); the library's RJ45 parts are the 13.2 mm housing, which cannot fit between the two captions. The housing is set with its foot on the \"1G\" line at y 35.0, and the three captions above are lowered 1.1 mm to clear it. The opening the housing frames is where the photograph shows the jack to within that."},"jacks":{"note":"L76 and docs/rj45-family-design.md settle which part each jack is: an Ethernet jack is common/rj45-eth@1 and a console or timing jack is std/rj45@2. CON is the console, so it is the std part; MGMT and CTRL are the two 1GB management ports the datasheet counts, so they are the Ethernet part. All three were std/rj45@2 in the first draft and the rule caught it. THE TWO ETHERNET JACKS ARE FITTED TAB UP and the console jack is not: the photograph reads MGMT's and CTRL's contacts along the bottom of the opening with the latch slot above, and CON's the other way about. Declared as rotate 180, because a jack fitted the other way up is the same jack turned over rather than a reflection of it, and its lamps really do change sides."},"layout":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"photo-measured - working/intake/maiaedge/pbc/photos/pbc-front-faceon.jpg (the maintainer, 2026-09-21), the first square-on view of this face, which closed the `front-face-positions` gap v4 carried. Deskewed 0.93 degrees and scaled PER AXIS: 4.004 px/mm across on the smooth body between the textured ears (437.9 mm), 4.139 down on the face's own edges (41.27). The 3.4% between them is the photograph's aspect, not the hardware's; the vertical figure checks against the USB opening's standard 12.0 mm to 2.5%. Read on those scales: the windows (see maiaedge/pbc-2000-bezel@2), the two 100G cages at x 40.35 and 61.95 - a 21.6 mm pitch, not abutting as v4 drew them - with \"0\"/\"1\" printed above and \"100G\" below; the status slot at x 34.3 to 37.6; the USB opening at x 261.3; CON, MGMT and CTRL centred at 289.45, 316.15 and 342.35 on a 26.3 mm pitch (v4 had 35.7), each captioned above and the two Ethernet jacks \"1G\" below; the touch screen at x 373.5 to 416.9. EVERY FRONT POSITION v4 CARRIED WAS WRONG by 5 to 25 mm, which is what \"estimated\" meant."},"louvres":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"photo-measured - eight rows of horizontal slots in each window, 3.85 mm apart, in columns about 25.4 mm apart (left window) and 24.6 (right) with ribs about 2.5 mm wide between them. THE SLOTS STOP AT THE PORTS: full-width rows run above and below the ports, and beside and between the ports and jacks there are only short slots in the gaps. The counts v4 carried (eight by five) were right; the pitch, the slot width and the gaps were not measured until the face-on photograph."},"model-number":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"vendor documentation - www.maiaedge.io/getting-started (getting-started.pdf), Safety Information: \"The PBC-2000 is equipped with two redundant AC power inputs.\" THE DATASHEET AND THE MANAGEMENT UI BOTH SAY ONLY \"PBC\", which is what this device was first modelled as; the setup guide is the only source held that gives the number. A DCIM reads `model` as the identity, so it is the number and not the family."},"numbering":{"note":"MaiaEdge's own management UI (working/intake/maiaedge/pbc/renders/ui-port-view.png) numbers the two 100G ports 0 and 1, so the group is index-origin 0, and captions them 100G. It captions MGMT and CTRL 1G and CON not at all, and - independently of L76 - DRAWS CON AS A DIFFERENT JACK from the other two, which is the console-versus- Ethernet split the rule had already forced. A UI view is a schematic: it is taken here for what is on the face, in what order, and what the vendor calls it. No coordinate comes from it."},"port-lamps":{"note":"field knowledge (the maintainer, 2026-09-15) - ONE lamp per 100G port - and the face-on photograph now rules out where v4 drew it: above each cage is the printed \"0\" and \"1\", and there is no lamp there. The one lit opening near the ports is the slot left of port 0, in which the vendor's UI view draws a column of four lamps; those four are placed in it. Two of them may be the port lamps the maintainer counts, but nothing says which, so all four carry `for: chassis` and the separate port lamps v4 drew are gone. See gaps `front-indicator-meanings`."},"ports":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet page 3 - \"Dual 100GbE Ethernet (QSFP28)\", \"2x 1GB RJ45\" management, \"1x USB 2.0\", \"RJ45 115.2 kbps\" console. Confirmed on the hardware: the front photograph reads the three jacks' own silkscreen as CON, MGMT and CTRL, which is the console plus the two management ports the table counts. AND NOW STATED BY THE VENDOR IN PROSE, which is better than either: the setup guide (www.maiaedge.io/getting-started) describes the face directly - the front has \"two windows where the ports are exposed\"; the lefthand window has \"two 100G interfaces, numbered 0 and 1 from left to right\"; and in the righthand window, \"from left to right, you'll find a USB port (not currently used), a serial console port, a 10/100/1000 management port, and a 10/100/1000 control port\". It calls MGMT \"the PBC's center management port\" and CTRL \"rightmost port in the right window\". Every one of those matches what was modelled from the photograph and the UI view; the ORDER of this face is no longer an inference. The vendor's own word for the octagonal cutouts is `window`, which is what the decor already calls them. Note the guide rates the two jacks 10/100/1000 where the table says 1GB, and calls the USB port NOT CURRENTLY USED."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet page 3 - \"Internal: AC, DC\" with \"Redundant Power Supply: Yes\". The 550W per-supply figure is photo-measured: both modules carry a blue 550W label. The datasheet states no chassis draw, so none is recorded and L27 stands."},"rear":{"confidence":"photo-measured","note":"photo-measured - working/intake/maiaedge/pbc/photos/pbc-rear-faceon.jpg, square to the rear and out of the rack. Scaled per axis: 4.137 px/mm across on the body's 437.9 mm (x 98 to 1910), 3.925 down on its 41.27; the scale checks against a part of known width, each supply's cage reading 74.9 and 73.6 mm against the CRPS module's 73.5. Left to right: a steel strap with the ground stud (x 0 to 17.5), supply 1 (cage 17.8 to 92.7), a steel strap (92.7 to 107.3), supply 2 (107.3 to 180.9), and the fan tray from 182.1 to the right edge. THE POSITIONS v4 TOOK FROM pbc-rear-b.jpeg WERE WRONG by up to 14 mm - in the rack, the side rails widened what was taken for the chassis. The whole rear is bare steel. The supplies and the fan tray are field-replaceable, each in its own bay; the supplies are maiaedge/pbc-2000-psu-550w@1, whose face - handle along the foot, inlet in a black shroud, tall purple latch - is not common/psu-550w@2's."},"size":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - MaiaEdge-PBC-PCE-Datasheet-v3.pdf page 3, \"Chassis (H x W x D) 1.625 x 17.24 x 11.46 in\" = 41.27 x 437.90 x 291.08 mm. THE ROW BELOW IT, \"Total (With Ears and Tabs) 1.625 x 19.02 x 12.13 in\", is NOT the chassis and is not modelled: 19.02 in is 483.11 mm, the rack face including the ears, and L43 exists because a device was once modelled wearing its flanges."},"thermal":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet page 3 - \"Internal fan-based forced-air cooling. Front-to-Back (F2B) - intake at front bezel / port side, exhaust at rear (fan/PSU side).\""},"usb":{"note":"the bare std/usb-a@1 receptacle, not the bezelled common/usb-a-bezel@1. That part wraps the opening in a silver plate spanning the component so it can abut its neighbours' bezels, which is the S9510-28DC's face; here the photograph shows a narrow slot straight through the faceplate with no plate around it. THE TONGUE IS WHITE BECAUSE THE PORT IS USB 2.0: page 3 says \"1x USB 2.0\", and USB-IF colours the Type-A insulator by what the port is - white for 2.0, blue for 3.0. The part could only draw the blue one, so it grew a `usb2` skin and this device asks for it. The photograph agrees as far as it can: the slot shows a pale tongue against a dark opening, and nothing
